main_text.l: riæ eius sunt differentiæ, propterea uaria à
nobis proponenda erunt remedia. Idcircò
quæ à sanguine crasso & melancholico or-
ta est, copiosiore, & frequentiore sanguinis
missione indiget, quàm quæ ab adusta bile
nascitur: & hæc adhuc, magis quá reliquæ,
quę quidem catharticis phlegmagogis, po-
tius profligari postulant. Igitur Galenus
commentario in Aphorismum quadrage-
simum septimum, Sectionis septimę nō de
postremarum curatione uerba fecit, sed de
his, quæ à fece sanguinis, & bile torrefacta
originem duxêre, dū incipientem elephant-
iasim se sanasse ait, primo quidem uenæ
sectione & purgatione: dein uerò singulis
annis pharmacum melanagogum propi-
nans. De ijsdem loquuntur Cornelius Cel-
sus, Paulus Ægineta, & Aëtius, qui non so-
lùm melanagogum præscribunt, sed & phle-
botomiam sæpe repetitam. Propterea dū
Cornelius protinus inter initia sanguinem
esse mittendum per biduum præcipit, cum
de sanguinea elephantia loquitur: cùm ue-
rò ueratro nigro uentrem esse soluendum
ait, cum etiam biliosam intelligit, quæ po-
tius catharticum, quàm phlebotomiam po-
stulat, propterea quòd in hac genuini san-
guinis

page.notes: The text is set in a long-s typeface where s looks like f; all such letters are transcribed as s. Line-end words without a printed hyphen (e.g. "po|stulat", "quadrage-simum" with its hyphen kept) are written whole or with the printed hyphen. The catchword is printed only as "guinis" at the right; the rest of the word lies on the line above, so only the visible part is given. The printed "melanagogum" in the second sentence is transcribed as printed. No headings, no notes in the margins.
